sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Registro Público de Panamá; unitary national incorporation regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil law codification with strong common law commercial, trust and transactional overlay; unitary national system, no material sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 31 October 2012)
United Kingdom–Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (1983, continued in force)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as reformed by Ley 41 de 2013; core provisions include Articles 1, 3, 6, 13, 18, 19, 22, 23, 24 and 30, supplemented by Public Registry regulations on foundation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Persons Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado) together with Foundation Regulations (Reglamento), presented as a notarized public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required; the foundation must be endowed with sufficient assets to fulfill its purpose, and an initial endowment of at least US$10,000 is market practice. There is no escrow account requirement; endowment may be subscribed in the Charter without immediate physical contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF is duly incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Panama by virtue of the registered Foundation Charter. The initial endowment of USD 10,000 is subscribed and allocated to the lawful purpose of wholesale remarketing of used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers. The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Charter, Panama. The Foundation Council is appointed, with named officers authorized to act individually and collectively, to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts, and administrate the foundation until the first beneficiary designation. This Resolution is effective immediately and recorded in the foundation minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and notarize the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notario Público) with protocolization before the Public Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian notary to prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish, including the foundation name, initial endowment, purpose, registered office, Council members, and beneficiary provisions. The Charter and optional Regulations must be executed before a notary and protocolized in the notarial protocol for submission to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Proposed Foundation Charter and Regulations
Notarized Power of Attorney of the Founder or corporate resolution if the founder is a legal entity
Copy of passports or corporate registry extracts of founder and initial Council members
Statement of purpose and asset declaration
Registration fee proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry returns the deed due to clerical omissions or missing signatures, correct and re-present the same deed within five business days; if substantive legal objections are raised, obtain legal counsel to amend the Charter and execute a corrected public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the protocolized notarial deed and the required supporting documents at the Public Registry counter or via the online user platform. Pay the official registration tariff and obtain the stamped Marginal Note and certificate of registration. Verify that the foundation name is reserved and accepted and that the foundation's registration number is recorded.
required_dossiers: Protocolized Notarial Deed of Constitution
Notarized Spanish-language translation of any non-Spanish document
Registry application form
Proof of payment of notarial and registry fees
Power of Attorney for the representative handling the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for inconsistency in the deed, submit a corrective addendum ('aclaración') or execute a new notarial deed. If the name is rejected, select alternate names and file a name reservation request before re-presenting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain taxpayer identification and commercial registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Public Registry registration, complete the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application online or in person at DGI. Attach the Foundation Charter and Public Registry certificate. The foundation will receive a Panamanian tax identification number and will register for territorial income tax, ITBMS, and dividend/withholding obligations as applicable. Also notify DGI of the economic activity code corresponding to ISIC 4659.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter and Public Registry Certificate
Valid identification of the Foundation Council members
RUC application form (Formulario de Inscripción)
Proof of registered office address (utility bill or lease contract)
Image or e-mail address for DGI notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI reports missing or inconsistent address evidence, provide a certified lease agreement or landlord letter within 10 business days. If the ISIC code is in dispute, supply the notarized business scope description and the import/export registration from Aduanas to reclassify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure municipal operating permit and municipal tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of the registered seat (typically Municipio de Panamá) – Dirección de Aviso de Operación.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the 'Aviso de Operación' at the corresponding Municipality for the physical office and/or equipment storage yard. Pay the municipal business tax based on the declared capital. Present the RUC certificate and proof of property occupancy or lease. The permit is renewed annually.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Public Registry Foundation certificate
Lease contract or ownership title of the physical premises
Municipal application form and payment receipt
Fire safety inspection certificate if premises are used for storage or offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires a zoning or usos de suelo certificate, obtain it from the Dirección de Desarrollo Urbano and submit the additional paperwork within 15 business days. Pay any outstanding municipal tax installments to lift suspension.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Social Security and occupational risk system
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) – Dirección de Afiliación y Registro, plus Dirección General de Riesgos Profesionales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the foundation will have employees, register the foundation as an employer with the CSS, file the employer and employee registration forms, and subscribe to the occupational-risk insurance coverage. If the foundation has no employees, no CSS employer registration is required; however, any physical workers in the storage yard must be enrolled before operations begin.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and Public Registry certificate
Employer registration application (form CSS 15-03)
Employee identity and payroll declarations
Proof of occupational-risk insurance or self-insurance approval
Description of workplace activities and site address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CSS reports missing payroll records or medical evaluation forms, correct the forms and resubmit within five business days to avoid employer surcharges; occupational-risk classification can be appealed through the CSS revision committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas, in coordination with the Municipality for the Aviso de Operación; import/export of used machinery is also coordinated through the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación para Casa de Representación y Almacén de Maquinaria Pesada Usada (Municipal Operating License) and, where applicable, MICI commercial registration certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Impact Assessment Registration for storage, wholesale transfer, and limited maintenance of used heavy machinery, with a standalone environmental impact study required only if the operation includes dismantling, fuel storage, or major mechanical repairs (Category II).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If wastewater is generated, compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 100 de 2000 maximum permissible discharge limits for oily wastewater and suspended solids to sewers or receiving bodies; if equipment painting or VOCs occur, comply with Panamanian air emission standards and the national VOC thresholds under the Reglamento de Emisiones de Fuentes Fijas; hazardous waste including used oils and batteries must be managed by licensed carriers and disposed of in facilities approved by MiAMBIENTE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios from the Dirección de Seguridad Civil y Bomberos of the local municipality; structural load inspection certificate for storage yards and office floors from the municipal engineering department; occupational safety and health clearance from the CSS Dirección General de Riesgos Profesionales and, where applicable, the Dirección General de Trabajo, covering heavy equipment handling and staff safety protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; official portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity acting through a Panamanian registered agent or legal representative must: (1) file the corresponding pre-registration form with the DGI, either online or through the taxpayer service office; (2) provide a certified copy of the entity's constitutive documents translated into Spanish, with notarization and Apostille or consular legalization as applicable; (3) execute and notarize a power of attorney appointing a resident agent; (4) submit a sworn affidavit identifying the business activity and the applicable Panama-source income and tax obligations; (5) obtain the provisional RUC, after which the DGI conducts a review, issues the permanent RUC certificate, and activates the taxpayer's electronic fiscal profile; and (6) request the fiscal authorization for electronic invoicing and, if required, the digital signature certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available. Panama applies a territorial taxation model under which any legal entity, including a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), may elect to be taxed as a small taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) if annual gross turnover is equal to or below B/.36,000. A PIF that carries out no commercial acts may remain outside the ITBMS and income tax nets; a PIF engaged in active trading of used machinery is treated as a general taxpayer at the corporate income tax rate of 25% on Panama-source profits. Mixed sourcing rules apply and no double tax relief treaty network is relied upon for export operations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, Panama's VAT-like transfer tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold; all persons engaged in the commercial transfer of tangible movable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS irrespective of turnover. An optional small-taxpayer regime permits filing and remittance on a simplified basis for annual taxable turnover up to B/.36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama requires mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI-approved system (Facturación Electrónica). Taxpayers must transmit each invoice and credit note in UBL 2.1 XML format to the DGI in real time, obtain a digital fiscal seal (stamping) with an associated QR code, and publish accepted documents in the DGI's centralized electronic registry. All transactions, including exports, must be reflected in the electronic clearance platform; intermediate software providers and taxpayers themselves must use DGI-authorized API integrations or fiscal DSPs. The issuance of a non-electronic invoice is treated as a procedural infringement and may invalidate the corresponding input credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS applies to used construction excavators if: (i) the goods are physically exported from Panama, evidenced by the customs unit load and bill of lading; (ii) title, ownership, and risk in the goods pass to a foreign buyer not resident in Panama; (iii) the sale is concluded under a purchase order or agreement issued by an offshore purchaser; and (iv) the consideration is received in a bank account outside Panama or through a licensed Panamanian bank in a clearing arrangement. Export-related services such as inland freight from Panama premises to the Panamanian port, inspection, and customs brokerage may also be zero-rated when directly linked to the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted and stamped by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá
Bill of Lading or airway bill identifying the foreign receiver and Panama port of departure
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire/SWIFT confirmation demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds from abroad
Commercial invoice and packing list issued electronically with DGI fiscal seal
Purchase agreement or purchase order with the foreign customer
Fumigation or phytosanitary certificate where required for used machinery
DGI Form 302 for export zero-rating evidence, if specifically requested during audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and customs authorities conduct joint audits of export zero-rating claims. Failure to maintain possession or timely submission of export evidence, or the absence of genuine foreign payment, results in retroactive clawback of all zero-rated VAT benefits, reassessment of the full 7% ITBMS on each invoice, and monetary surcharge of 10% per month of assessed tax (up to 100%). Additionally, penalties equal to 50% of the tax fraudulently omitted may be imposed, civil fines per false customs declaration and unauthorized electronic seal apply, and criminal liability may arise under Panama's Tax Procedure Code and Criminal Code, including jail terms for aggravated evasion. The taxpayer's digital invoicing authorization and export zero-rating eligibility may be suspended for a period of one to three years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No Panamanian central bank exists; the US Dollar is legal tender under the 1904 Monetary Agreement and Decree 74 of 2004. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the sole banking and AML/CFT regulator, supervising banks and financial institutions. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent and clearing administrator for the State, but does not set monetary policy or issue currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full official dollarization: the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) exists only as a 1:1 unit-of-account with USD coins; Federal Reserve notes circulate exclusively. There is no exchange-control law, no capital-account restriction, no prior-authorization requirement for FX conversion, and no restriction on the free movement of USD capital, dividends, or profits. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible by statute and practice; profit remittance is tax-exempt at source under Panama's territorial tax system, and no dividends withholding applies to distribution to non-resident beneficiaries provided the PIF has satisfied annual franchise tax and economic substance filings under Law 254 of 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama has never enacted an export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion regime. Proceeds from the export of used construction machinery are freely retainable in USD, payable into any onshore or offshore USD account, or immediately disbursed. For bank credit of export proceeds the commercial bank typically requires the SIGA export declaration (Declaración de Mercancías) with the equipment serial numbers, the commercial invoice, and the ocean bill of lading; however this is a documentary KYC practice, not a legal surrender obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Moderate. Panama enacted a Payment Institutions licensing regime under SBP Agreement No. 006-2023, which subjects any EMI-like activity to a full SBP license. Unlicensed offshore EMIs (EU/UK digital banks) may open a non-resident USD account to receive proceeds from international auction platforms, but cannot serve as the primary treasury settlement node because Law 254 of 2020 economic substance principles require the PIF's core treasury activity to be visible in Panama. The viable architecture is: offshore EMI as a collection-only side-purse for eBay/Ritchie Bros./IronPlanet payouts, with a 24-72 hour sweep to the Panamanian licensed bank; the domestic licensed account remains the operational and compliance nexus.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is a de facto mandate for non-resident PIF signatories. While SBP Agreement 005-2022 permits remote verification for 'trusted channel' clients, in practice every Panamanian bank requires at least one physical sit-down at the foundation office or bank branch for the first account opening. The founder, the foundation council president, and the authorized treasury signatory must appear before a Panamanian notary and the bank's compliance officer. Subsequent onboarding can be conducted through the resident domiciliary agent. Remote opening is legally possible under the SBP's remote KYC provisions if the PIF already holds a validated economic substance file and the founder has an existing banking relationship with the same institution in Panama, but interview attendance is mandated if the RUAF beneficial-owner list contains any politically exposed person or if the machine-trading counterparty resides in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF legal form flagged as potential anonymity vehicle under FATF Recommendation 25 and SBP Circular 005-2022 enhanced due diligence for private interest foundations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Acto Constitutivo) with the stated commercial purpose expressly limited to wholesale remarketing of used heavy machinery under ISIC 4659/NAICS 423810; RUAF beneficial-owner registration certificate issued under Law 23 of 2015; notarized and apostilled current list of Foundation Council members; a signed Economic Substance Declaration under Law 254 of 2020 demonstrating physical administration office, local domiciliary agent, and Panamanian accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Used hydraulic excavators classified as high-value movable goods with inherent risk of invoice manipulation, undocumented parts, or stolen-machine title laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full asset chain-of-custody file per unit: OEM serial number and engine number, prior-title or auction certificate, original supplier invoice, third-party pre-export inspection certificate (Bureau Veritas/Intertek/SGS) verifying machine identification, and the SIGA customs export declaration. For each inbound credit, the bank receives an automated reference containing the unique machine serial number matched to the underlying commercial invoice and bill of lading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty funds originate from buyers in developing Latin American and African jurisdictions with limited AML enforcement, creating suspicion of layered source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negotiated Treasury Payment Policy document: (i) all inbound buyer wires must reference the specific machine serial number and the signed purchase agreement; (ii) the buyer's bank must issue a professional bank reference letter confirming the buyer's operational standing; (iii) any single wire exceeding USD 250,000 is accompanied by a completed Source of Funds questionnaire and the buyer's tax-existence certificate; (iv) the PIF commits to no cash transactions and no third-party payments without an expressed written instruction in the purchase agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US export-control and OFAC screening risk: used excavators contain diesel engines and electronic control units subject to US BIS (EAR 15 CFR 730-774) re-export controls, and the PIF wiring network may touch countries under US sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dense compliance package: a country-of-origin matrix per machine (US/EU/JP/KR origin), a written EAR re-export attestation stating the end-user and end-use for each transaction, an OFAC/UN/EU/UK sanctions-list screening log executed at contract signature, the bank's assigned sanctions filtering internal ID for the PIF, and a bilingual (English/Spanish) corporate AML manual approved by the SBP-regulated bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Governance mismatch: The individuals appointed to the Foundation Council may not coincide with the RUAF registered ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Beneficial Ownership Concordance Statement confirming the RUAF registrant's position as the exclusive economic settlor with veto rights over large treasury disbursements; the Foundation Council's unanimous Resolution delegating treasury signing authority to a name-checked signatory; Panama sworn-translator Spanish/English versions attached to all banking applications; a detailed organizational chart initialed by the compliance officer during onboarding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for initial capital: SWIFT MT103 from the founder's foreign bank to the PIF's Panama Capital Escrow Account, with Field 70 (Remittance Information) reading 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION STATUTE ARTICLE [_X_] – FOUNDER ID [_name_]'; supporting upload of the notarized foundation statute, the RUAF certificate, and the founder's bank reference letter. For recurring trade proceeds: MT103 must include in Field 70 the commercial invoice number plus the used-equipment serial number; the bank's trade operations unit verifies the file against the pre-registered purchase agreement, SIGA export declaration, and bill of lading. For incoming SWIFT wires in non-USD currencies (EUR, JPY, GBP), the Panamanian receiving bank automatically converts at its desk rate; to avoid spread-added execution, the PIF instructs the sending bank to pre-convert into USD at the originating bank's rate before issuing the MT103, therefore the SBP-regulated Panama account receives only USD for final clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 (OBI, Originator-to-Beneficiary Instruction) with matched reference to supplier name and machine purchase order, executed from the Panama Operational Account through the bank's New York correspondent (typically Bank of New York Mellon / Citibank / JPMorgan) with T+0/T+1 USD finality. For high-value used-equipment acquisitions from auction houses (Ritchie Bros., IronPlanet) and OEM rebuild centers, the PIF uses irrevocable commercial documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) governed by UCP 600, issued by its Panamanian bank in favor of the supplier, payable against presentation of the commercial invoice, full set clean on-board bill of lading, packing list, and an independent inspection certificate. In-country disbursements (domiciliary agent, warehouse fees, transport within Panama) clear via Panama's national ACH/SPI retail clearing with MICR routing, linked to the same USD account without any conversion event.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EUR and USD/JPY forward contracts with SBP-licensed commercial banks, underlying payables for European and Japanese used-excavator sourcing (auction house settlement in EUR/JPY).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in COP, MXN, BRL, CLP and PEN, hedgeable against forecast USD receivables from Latin American buyers; NDFs are universally used in Panama's dollarized system because no local market exists for the Latin American currencies.

Cross-currency basis swaps (USD vs EUR, USD vs JPY) on notional amounts matching confirmed multi-unit sourcing contracts; transacted with the treasury desk of the primary relationship bank under ISDA/CSA documentation.

Interest rate swaps on USD SOFR floating-rate debt, if the PIF's trade-finance line or LC discounting facilities carry floating exposure; permissible without SBP licensing because the corporate executes through a licensed counterparty bank.
Simple USD/PAB currency symmetry is not required: Balboa exists only as coins and is pegged 1:1 with USD, therefore no intra-Panama FX hedge is needed or possible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Maintenance Tax (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, remitted through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March; calendar-year deadline applicable to all Panamanian private interest foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late remittance attracts statutory surcharge plus accumulated interest; failure to cure for 12 consecutive months after formal notice leads to administrative strike-off of the foundation from the Public Registry, with reinstatement requiring payment of arrears and restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and AML Confirmation Letter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident agent (non-governmental; required under Panamanian AML Law No. 23 of 2015)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March, synchronized with the annual maintenance payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-responsive foundation council triggers a mandatory AML client-due-diligence review; persistent failure permits the resident agent to resign, causing the foundation to lose its statutory registered office and face strike-off procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Conditional DGI Income Tax Return (Renta) — only for Panamanian-source gross income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI / Sistema Tu Empresa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 15 March following the close of the calendar tax year (1 January – 31 December); not required when the foundation has only non-Panamanian-source trading income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the foundation to DGI non-compliance penalties of a statutory percentage per month of delay, plus interest; continued evasion can result in tax administrative seizure and filing inertia.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private interest foundation is exempt from filing audited financial statements with Panamanian authorities when its activities generate only foreign-source income. A compulsory independent audit is triggered only if (i) the foundation’s charter or a beneficiary requires an audit, or (ii) the foundation engages in Panamanian-source taxable activities and its gross annual revenue exceeds the DGI audit threshold of USD 300,000, in which case audited statements must be presented to the DGI.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Internal accounting records are mandatory under Law No. 25 of 1995 and Law No. 52 of 2016; where formal financial statements are produced, the applicable framework is the NIIF/NIF issued by the Panamanian Association of Accountants (IFRS for SMEs for non-listed entities; full IFRS for entities exceeding the audit threshold).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law No. 23 of 2015 and the financial information regime, the resident agent must maintain current beneficial ownership data. The foundation council must submit an annual written confirmation (or updated information) of every foundation member, council member, protector and direct beneficiary; this confirmation must be provided to the resident agent together with the annual tax payment by 31 March of each year. The information remains confidential and is not filed with the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,500 per year for licensed resident agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 9,000 per year for a conditional independent audit of a used-machinery trading foundation; USD 1,000 – USD 2,500 for preparing internal accounting records without statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Panama-source net taxable income only; territorial income tax system)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for Private Interest Foundations. Foreign-source income is exempt under Panamanian territoriality, giving an effective 0% rate on non-Panamanian commercial gains, while Panama-source trading income is taxed at 25%. No Colon Free Zone or Panama-Pacifico incentive applies unless separately licensed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: DGI Form 400 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto Sobre la Renta), filed electronically through the 'T@x Panama' DGI portal; mandatory for all legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations carrying on taxable Panamanian-source activity.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal year follows the calendar year unless an alternative 12-month period is authorised by the DGI. Quarterly advance tax payments are separately required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed and any residual tax paid within three months after fiscal year-end, i.e. by 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number assigned by the DGI upon registration of the Private Interest Foundation through its resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders must ensure the Panamanian resident agent has authority to obtain the RUC, access the T@x Panama portal, and file the electronic declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable period covered, normally 1 January to 31 December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled PIFs must align the Panamanian fiscal period to the calendar year absent prior DGI approval of a non-standard period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic activity code: ISIC 4659, wholesale of used construction machinery and equipment; annotate 'secondhand hydraulic excavators and rollers' (NAICS 423810).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF is engaged in active trading, do not select 'passive asset holding' or 'private foundation exempt activity'; erroneous classification is a trigger for economic substance and transfer pricing review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panamanian-source trading, commissions, brokerage and sales of used excavators physically delivered or title-passed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue may be excluded under territoriality, but must be shown on the reconciliation annex with documentary support to avoid a DGI recharacterisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred for the generation of taxed Panama-source income: acquisition cost of used excavators, freight, marine insurance, repair and reconditioning costs, broker commissions, inspection fees and allocated overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases from related suppliers are deductible only if priced at arm's length and accompanied by local transfer pricing documentation if the threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses from prior fiscal years applied against current taxable income, up to the five-year carryforward limit and any statutory annual caps.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a loss carryforward schedule and tax reconciliation computation; no carryback of losses is permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment subject the taxpayer to an administrative fine of USD 100 to USD 10,000 depending on the amount of tax involved, plus a monthly surcharge of 5% on the unpaid tax (maximum 50%) and statutory delay interest at approximately 1.5% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends or profit distributions paid from Panamanian corporate income tax profits; 10% on dividends or beneficiary distributions made from profits that were not subject to Panamanian ISR (for example, foreign-source income or exempt income).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must hold a current Panamanian-source recognized Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction and submit it, together with a DTA self-certification, to the Panamanian withholding agent before the remittance. The withholding agent files the corresponding annex on Form 400; if treaty relief was applied at source, the DGI may require additional exchange-of-information verification. For refunds, a 'Solicitud de Devolución' must be filed with the DGI within the statutory limitation period, with proof of economic substance and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 15% gross on Panama-source royalties and technology/technical assistance fees paid to non-residents; 5% gross on interest paid to foreign lenders. Applicable Double Taxation Treaties may reduce royalties to 10% and interest to 5%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and holds a current tax residence certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 250,000 (Panamanian Balboa at parity with USD) or more in related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory local file documentation and the annual transfer pricing disclosure. Group master file and country-by-country reporting obligations arise for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above PAN 250 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Decree Law 111 of 2020) require any tax-resident Panamanian entity performing a 'relevant activity' to show real physical presence, local employment, effective management and risk control in Panama, and to file an annual economic substance report. Active purchase and resale of used construction machinery is regarded as a distribution and service centre activity; therefore the PIF must demonstrate substantive Panamanian substance and not merely a registered address.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Panama-source sales proceeds from used excavators, fabricating supplier invoices, inflating deductible COGS through non-arm's-length related parties, or claiming treaty exemptions without beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI reassessment with accrued surcharges; administrative fine of 50% up to 300% of the omitted tax; seizure of bank accounts and assets; mandatory criminal referral to the Public Prosecutor's Office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and directors who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and civil restitution; criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to five years, judicial travel bans, disqualification from holding Panamanian director or resident agent positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Private Interest Foundation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a letter-box entity with no board meetings in Panama, no accounting records, no local economic substance, and using the foundation solely to channel foreign trading profits of a high-tax-resident ultimate owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic substance penalties, loss of territorial tax benefits, mandatory automatic exchange of financial account and foundation information, denial of tax residency certificates, and cancellation of the foundation's beneficial-ownership registry licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent may be held civilly liable for the principal's unpaid taxes; administrative travel bans and prohibition orders may be imposed; criminal convictions for sham facilitation carry imprisonment penalties of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and AML Infractions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF to invoice used construction excavators through SWIFT letters of credit with inflated or understated prices, false bills of lading, duplicate or phantom inspections, or routing sale proceeds through shell accounts to conceal beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal asset confiscation (extinción de dominio), fines of two to five times the laundered value, revocation of foundation registration, and cross-reporting by DGI and the Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit to the Public Prosecutor's Office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, trustees and beneficial owners face imprisonment of up to twelve years under Panama's money-laundering provisions, preventive seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and permanent director disqualification.
